title: Single-tank transfer sequence understanding
narrative:
Explicit entities from 01_single_tank_transfer_description.txt are Operator, Controller, Tank 1, Tank 2, Inlet valve, Transfer valve, Drain valve, High-level switch, Low-level switch, and the commands START, STOP, and SHUT. Tank 1 and Tank 2 are both described as atmospheric liquid tanks. The notes state that Tank 1 is connected to Tank 2 by the inlet valve, transfer valve, and drain valve. This establishes a stated connection among the two tanks and the three valves, but the exact per-valve flow topology is not further specified in the notes. The Controller is implied to control the Inlet valve, Transfer valve, and Drain valve. The Operator explicitly issues START, STOP, and SHUT commands. The High-level switch explicitly senses Tank 1 level. The Low-level switch explicitly senses Tank 1 level and also explicitly senses Tank 2 level; the notes use one name for low-level sensing on both tanks and do not distinguish whether this is one shared logical element name or two separate low-level switches, one per tank.

The sequence behavior explicitly established is as follows. On START, the Controller fills Tank 1 until Tank 1 reaches its High-level switch. After Tank 1 High-level switch is reached, the Controller waits 10 seconds. After that 10-second wait, the Controller transfers liquid to Tank 2 until Tank 1 reaches its Low-level switch. After Tank 1 Low-level switch is reached, the Controller waits 10 seconds. After this second 10-second wait, the Controller drains Tank 2 until Tank 2 reaches its Low-level switch. STOP behavior is explicit: when STOP is issued, every valve closes and the sequence pauses. A later START resumes the interrupted state rather than restarting from the beginning. SHUT behavior is explicit: when SHUT is issued, the inlet is inhibited and the transfer and drain paths are opened until both tanks are empty. The notes do not explicitly define command priority when STOP and SHUT compete, nor do they define whether SHUT is resumable.

The notes explicitly require that the model report tank levels and valve commands for a 900-second experiment. No explicit simulation start time, integration intervals, or numerical tolerance are stated. No explicit equations, conservation relationships, valve flow laws, tank geometries, initial tank levels, switch threshold values, or acceptance checks are provided in the notes. Derived from the described sequence and the requirement to report tank levels, the system is a batch_sequential_process involving liquid storage and transfer, with fluid level behavior present; however, continuous hydraulic relationships are not specified in the notes and should not be invented.

The sequence uses a low-level condition on Tank 1 during transfer and a low-level condition on Tank 2 during drain. This creates a material modeling ambiguity about whether there are two physical switches with the same generic name or one logical signal name reused for different tanks.
